result: For EVERY complex rank-four Bob map K:C^5->C^4 whose kernel lies in span{|0>,|3>}, the normalized compression of the specified 4x5 PPT/SN3 grid state has Schmidt number <=2. It is exactly 2 unless ker(K)=span{|0>}; at that endpoint only <=2 is claimed. An explicit rational-function decomposition applies uniformly to all complex parameters. A verified exact local symmetry gives the analogous statements for kernel lines in span{|2>,|4>}, with the exceptional endpoint span{|2>}.
state: Use the same R and notation as frontier-20261028-grid-state-five-projections-v1.json SHA256 9863760e2ca2331164d12e62300f3ad7db5b6a17a3ef424e360d504d541004a9: R=[A]+[B]+[D]+3([C]+[E]+[F]+[G]+[I]+[H]), with A=|00>+|11>+|22>, B=|01>+|12>, D=|10>-|21>, C=|02>+|34>, E=|20>+|33>, F=|23>, G=|30>, I=|32>, H=|04>. R/31 is PPT and SN3 by the prior explicit certificates, based on the range in https://arxiv.org/html/2509.07086v1 Eq.11. No source priority or novelty is claimed.
normal_form: The images of Bob labels 1,2,4 and the common image line of 0,3 are linearly independent. Thus, up to invertible output filtering, K sends |0>->u|0>, |3>->v|0>, while |1>,|2> remain themselves and |4>->|3>, with (u,v)!=(0,0). Write R_uv for the unnormalized local compression. Invertible local filters preserve PPT and Schmidt number.
phase_seed: For each z in {1,i,-1,-i}, q_z=zA'+B'-z^2 D'-z^3 u|20>. Its Alice coefficient row 2 equals z times row 1, and row 3 is zero; hence SR(q_z)<=2 for all complex u. The four-phase sum is (1/4)sum_z[q_z]=[A']+[B']+[D']+|u|^2[20], with all off-diagonal phase terms canceled.
positive_residual: Set U=|u|^2,V=|v|^2 and X=2U+3V>0. The residual 3([E']+[F']+[G'])-U[20] acts only on Bob |0>, and in Alice basis |2>,|3> is the Hermitian matrix [[2U+3V,3u conjugate(v)],[3 conjugate(u)v,3(U+V)]]. Put t=3 conjugate(u)v/X and delta=(6U^2+6UV+9V^2)/X>=0. Exact identity: residual = X[|20>+t|30>]+delta[30]. Both are product projectors.
complete_decomposition: R_uv=(1/4)sum_(z^4=1)[q_z]+3([C']+[I']+[H'])+X[|20>+t|30>]+delta[30]. Every q_z has SR<=2, C' has SR<=2, and the other terms are products, with all coefficients nonnegative for any nonzero (u,v). Therefore SN(R_uv)<=2. PPT follows from the explicit R^Gamma certificate and local complete positivity, including complex u,v.
entanglement_when_u_nonzero: Project further to Alice 0,1,2 and output Bob 0,1,2. The resulting state has range [[u*a,b,c],[u*d,a,b],[e,-d,a]], with arbitrary complex a,b,c,d,e, and contains the vector u|00>+|11>+|22> (a=1). For a rank-one range vector, the two 2x2 minors are u(a^2-bd) and a^2+bd. If u!=0 both vanish only when a=0. Thus the 3x3 state is entangled by the range criterion, so its 4x4 parent is entangled; combined with the decomposition this gives SN=2. When u=0 the proof only gives SN<=2; it does not assert separability or entanglement.
reflection_symmetry: Define local unitaries on basis states S_A: |0>->-|2>, |1>->|1>, |2>->|0>, |3>->|3>; S_B: |0>->-|2>, |1>->|1>, |2>->|0>, |3>->-|4>, |4>->-|3>. They send A->A, B->D, D->-B, C->-E, E->-C, F->-H, G->-I, I->G, H->F, so (S_A tensor S_B)R(S_A tensor S_B)^*=R. S_B maps span{|0>,|3>} onto span{|2>,|4>}; therefore the same SN<=2 theorem holds on that family, and its states are entangled except possibly when the kernel is span{|2>}.

verification.observed: Five exact Gaussian-rational pairs (u,v)=(1,0),(0,1),(1,2),(1+i,1-i),(i,3): each checks all four rank-two phase vectors by all 3x3 minors and all 256 entries of the projector identity, with zero mismatches. The source local symmetry was independently checked at all 400 state entries, zero mismatches. All arithmetic is Fraction/Gaussian-rational.
verification.scope: The five numerical inputs are finite checks; all complex quantifiers follow from the written rank and Hermitian-residual proof above. No independent external or formal review is claimed.

limits: The result covers two additional CP1 kernel-line families, not arbitrary 5-to-4 projections or all 4x4 PPT states. It does not settle the u=0 endpoint's exact Schmidt number, provide a 4x4 SN>=3 witness, or establish novelty.
